story.title: The Sympathy Tax
story.logline: In a city where emotional tears have monetary value, a man tries to fake grief to pay his rent, only to discover his real tears are worth infinitely more.
story.theme: The commodification of genuine human emotion.
story.twist: The tears he shed while faking grief were actually triggered by the terrifying realization that he was truly losing his humanity.
story.ending: If your sorrow buys your survival, how do you ever know if your heart is actually broken?

scenes.narration: My tears just paid my electric bill. Do you know what it costs to cry on command?
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, a 25-year-old man with messy dark hair and a worn grey hoodie, standing in a sleek, dimly lit futuristic apartment, wiping a genuine tear off his cheek.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up tracking the tear falling onto a glowing payment scanner.

scenes.narration: The city meter reads your grief. Sad thoughts equal soft cash. Happy smiles leave you starving in the dark.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, same messy dark hair and grey hoodie, staring at a digital wall display showing his rapidly depleting balance of emotional currency.
scenes.camera: Static medium shot with neon reflections pulsing on the wall.

scenes.narration: I never felt a damn thing. I just watched old sad movies until my eyes leaked on the scanner.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, same dark hair and grey hoodie, sitting on a bare mattress, his glowing phone screen casting a blue light on his dry, tired face.
scenes.camera: Low angle pushing in slowly toward his face.

scenes.narration: Rent is due tomorrow. The standard heartbreak movie isn't cutting it anymore. My tear ducts are completely dry.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, same dark hair and grey hoodie, aggressively rubbing his eyes in front of a blank, dark payment terminal in his kitchen.
scenes.camera: Handheld shaky cam tracking his frustration.

scenes.narration: So I invented a tragedy. I imagined the absolute worst thing that could ever possibly happen to me.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, same dark hair and grey hoodie, closing his eyes tightly, his jaw clenched as he forces himself to visualize a nightmare.
scenes.camera: Slow zoom in on his tense, sweating face.

scenes.narration: I imagined holding someone I loved as they faded away, leaving me utterly alone in this cold world.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, same dark hair and grey hoodie, dropping to his knees on the floor, his arms wrapped tightly around his own empty chest.
scenes.camera: Overhead shot spinning slowly around him.

scenes.narration: The scanner beeped instantly. Green light flashed. A flood of currency poured into my digital wallet.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of the payment terminal turning bright emerald green, numbers rapidly climbing as a flood of heavy tears drips onto the glass.
scenes.camera: Macro shot focusing on the falling drops of water.

scenes.narration: I was rich. I could finally eat. But then I looked at the security camera footage on the wall.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, same dark hair and grey hoodie, rising slowly to his feet, staring in horror at a small wall monitor.
scenes.camera: Push in past his shoulder to the monitor screen.

scenes.narration: The system didn't pay me for faking. It paid me because for one second, I believed my own lie.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of the monitor showing replay footage of Leo crying, his expression entirely devoid of acting, revealing raw, unfiltered terror.
scenes.camera: Static tight shot on the glowing screen.

scenes.narration: I bought my dinner with a manufactured soul. If your sorrow buys survival, are you even human anymore?
scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of Leo, same dark hair and grey hoodie, standing alone in his dark apartment, staring blankly at the glowing green cash counter.
scenes.camera: Pull back slowly into darkness, framing him like a prisoner.

caption.hook: Crying just paid my rent today.
caption.title: The Sympathy Tax: A Price on Sorrow
caption.caption: In a city where sorrow is currency, I tried to fake my way out of poverty. But the moment I realized I had nothing left to feel, I finally understood the true cost of my humanity.
